issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class Farm: The problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 108-109) explicitly requires initializing the animals ArrayList "in a constructor with no arguments". The template's example Main (template repository src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 14) instantiates Farm using the no-argument constructor (new Farm()). The template Farm (template repository src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 3-4) currently has no constructors implemented. The solution implementation (solution repository src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 11-13) provides only a constructor with an int parameter (public Farm(int initialCapacity)) and no no-argument constructor. This inconsistency will cause code that expects a no-arg Farm() (as described in the spec and shown in the template Main) to fail to compile against the solution as provided.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor to Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g., public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). If an initial-capacity constructor is desired for extra functionality, keep it as an overload (public Farm(int initialCapacity) { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(initialCapacity); }). Update the solution repository to include the no-arg constructor (and optionally the int constructor) so that the problem statement, template Main, and solution are consistent.

issues.description: Constructor name/signature mismatch for the Farm class: the problem statement and template expect and instruct students to use a no-argument constructor Farm() that initializes the internal ArrayList (problem statement asks to “Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments” and the template Main.java instantiates the farm with new Farm()), but the solution implementation only provides a single constructor public Farm(int initialCapacity) (no no-arg overload). A student comparing artifacts will see Farm() in the problem/template and Farm(int) in the solution and be unable to directly map the required no-arg constructor to the solution code, causing confusion or preventing straightforward usage of the solution API.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a public no-argument constructor to the solution's Farm class that initializes the animals list, or overload the existing constructor. For example: public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } (this preserves the existing Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor while aligning the solution API with the problem description and the template usage).
